=== adding-content.md enchant section ===
81:- **A station with its own panel (not the recipe book)** — the **enchanting table**, the **anvil**, and the **grindstone** are the reference. Their interaction sets `state.craftingStation` to a new id, but that id goes on the **engine/UI** station union (`craftingStation` on `GameState` and `GameSnapshot`, and the `openedStation` event in `state.ts`, plus the `InventoryPanel` `craftingStation` prop) and **not** on `Recipe.station` — so `STATION_LABELS` (keyed off `Recipe.station`) needs no entry. The panel is a dedicated `*Column` component branched in before the recipe book in `InventoryPanel`, acting on the **selected hotbar slot** (`inventory[selectedHotbarSlot]`); its actions are new `Command`s in `commands.ts` handled in `GameEngine.dispatch` (gated on `state.craftingStation === <id>`), each emitting a one-shot event for the audio director. The block itself is **craft-only** (never generated), so adding the `BlockId` at the end of the enum needs **no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump** — just `BLOCK_COLORS` (atlas sizing), an atlas paint branch, the exhaustive `GROUP_BY_BLOCK`, and `BREAK_HARDNESS`/item-def/`BLOCK_TO_SLOT`/recipe.
125:## An enchantment (per-item gear modifier)
127:- Enchantments are **per-item-instance data, like durability** — they live on the `InventorySlot`'s `enchantments` field (`{ id, level }[]`), driven by `lib/game/enchantments.ts`. Add an id to the `EnchantmentId` union (`types.ts`), list it in `ENCHANTMENT_DEFS` (applicable item kinds + max level) and `ENCHANTMENT_ORDER`, and put magnitudes in `config.ts`.
129:- **Non-stackable for free**: enchantments only sit on durable gear, which is already stack-size 1 (`maxStackSizeForItem`), and `{ ...slot }` clones carry the field through every inventory move.
130:- **Apply it** with the `enchant` command (gated on an open enchanting table): `canEnchant` (kind + level cap) → `spendXpLevels` → immutable `applyEnchant`. The `EnchantingColumn` panel renders the options for the selected hotbar item.
131:- **Persist it**: enchantments are an **additive save field** on `SavedSlot` — see [save-format.md](save-format.md) (v7); `restoreSlot` validates them on load (known ids, clamped levels, durable gear only).
=== save-format.md mending/enchant ===
14:- inventory slots with durability, **enchantments, and a custom name** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments?, customName? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) and `customName` (the anvil rename) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known enchant ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`; `customName` trimmed and capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN`, blanks dropped). The same path serializes chest contents
15:- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
16:- equipped armor — the worn pieces themselves (one per slot, dedicated storage), persisted as per-slot `SavedSlot` via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor` (so worn durability/enchantments/customName survive). A worn piece lives **only** here, not in the 36 inventory slots
39:- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
40:- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
44:- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
53:- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → v10 → v11 → v12.

=== adding-content.md enchant section ===
81:- **A station with its own panel (not the recipe book)** — the **enchanting table**, the **anvil**, and the **grindstone** are the reference. Their interaction sets `state.craftingStation` to a new id, but that id goes on the **engine/UI** station union (`craftingStation` on `GameState` and `GameSnapshot`, and the `openedStation` event in `state.ts`, plus the `InventoryPanel` `craftingStation` prop) and **not** on `Recipe.station` — so `STATION_LABELS` (keyed off `Recipe.station`) needs no entry. The panel is a dedicated `*Column` component branched in before the recipe book in `InventoryPanel`, acting on the **selected hotbar slot** (`inventory[selectedHotbarSlot]`); its actions are new `Command`s in `commands.ts` handled in `GameEngine.dispatch` (gated on `state.craftingStation === <id>`), each emitting a one-shot event for the audio director. The block itself is **craft-only** (never generated), so adding the `BlockId` at the end of the enum needs **no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump** — just `BLOCK_COLORS` (atlas sizing), an atlas paint branch, the exhaustive `GROUP_BY_BLOCK`, and `BREAK_HARDNESS`/item-def/`BLOCK_TO_SLOT`/recipe.
125:## An enchantment (per-item gear modifier)
127:- Enchantments are **per-item-instance data, like durability** — they live on the `InventorySlot`'s `enchantments` field (`{ id, level }[]`), driven by `lib/game/enchantments.ts`. Add an id to the `EnchantmentId` union (`types.ts`), list it in `ENCHANTMENT_DEFS` (applicable item kinds + max level) and `ENCHANTMENT_ORDER`, and put magnitudes in `config.ts`.
129:- **Non-stackable for free**: enchantments only sit on durable gear, which is already stack-size 1 (`maxStackSizeForItem`), and `{ ...slot }` clones carry the field through every inventory move.
130:- **Apply it** with the `enchant` command (gated on an open enchanting table): `canEnchant` (kind + level cap) → `spendXpLevels` → immutable `applyEnchant`. The `EnchantingColumn` panel renders the options for the selected hotbar item.
131:- **Persist it**: enchantments are an **additive save field** on `SavedSlot` — see [save-format.md](save-format.md) (v7); `restoreSlot` validates them on load (known ids, clamped levels, durable gear only).
=== save-format.md mending/enchant ===
14:- inventory slots with durability, **enchantments, and a custom name** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments?, customName? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) and `customName` (the anvil rename) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known enchant ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`; `customName` trimmed and capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN`, blanks dropped). The same path serializes chest contents
15:- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
16:- equipped armor — the worn pieces themselves (one per slot, dedicated storage), persisted as per-slot `SavedSlot` via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor` (so worn durability/enchantments/customName survive). A worn piece lives **only** here, not in the 36 inventory slots
39:- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
40:- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
44:- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
53:- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → v10 → v11 → v12.

## Status effects

Timed buffs on the player (`lib/game/engine/systems/statusEffects.ts`); their
icon + countdown show top-left while active. Re-applying refreshes to the longer
remaining time; **all clear on death** but otherwise persist across a reload.

| Swiftness       | 3:00     | Potion (feather)    | Move ×1.2 faster                                       |

## XP & enchanting

XP banks as points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` = 10 points per level) and is spent at an
**enchanting table** to enchant the selected gear. XP is **kept across death**.
Source: `lib/game/engine/systems/xp.ts`, `lib/game/mobXp.ts`, `lib/game/enchantments.ts`.

### XP sources

| Source        | XP                                                       |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mob kill      | passives 1–2, hostiles 5, **boss 200**; babies give none |
| Mining ore    | coal 1, sliver 2, ruby/gold 4, sapphire 6, diamond 8     |
| Fishing catch | 2                                                        |

### Enchantments

Each costs **3 XP levels** per application, up to that enchantment's max level
(**3** for most, **1** for Mending), applied at the enchanting table to the
selected tool/weapon/armor. Enchantments are per-item and survive a save.

| Sharpness   | weapons             | +2 melee damage                                               |
| Protection  | armor               | +2 defense (more damage reduction)                            |
| Efficiency  | tools               | ×(1 + 0.3 × level) mining speed                               |
| Unbreaking  | tools/weapons/armor | 20% chance per level to skip wear                             |
| Mending     | tools/weapons/armor | gained XP repairs the gear (2 durability per XP); max level 1 |

file.content:
Spend it at an **enchanting table** (craft one from **2 diamond ore + 4 cobble**).
Place it, right-click to open the enchanting panel, then **select** the tool,
weapon, or armor you want to improve in your hotbar — the panel shows the
enchantments it can take. Each costs **3 levels** and can be applied up to **three
times**:

- **Sharpness** (weapons) — hit harder in melee
- **Protection** (armor) — take less damage
- **Efficiency** (tools) — mine faster
- **Unbreaking** (any gear) — gear lasts longer (it sometimes ignores wear)
- **Mending** (any gear) — XP you pick up repairs the held or worn item instead of
  banking, as long as it's damaged

Buttons grey out when you can't afford the cost or the enchant is maxed.
Enchantments are part of the item, so they're kept in chests and across reloads.
Full numbers are in the [reference](reference.md#xp--enchanting).

## The anvil

the anvil panel. Like the enchanting table it works on the **selected** hotbar
item — a tool, weapon, or armor piece — and spends XP levels:

content.content:
1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Fixed
8	
9	- **Equipped armor no longer occupies a hotbar/inventory slot.** Armor was equipped _by reference_ — the worn piece stayed in the inventory and kept occupying its slot (and rendered twice: once in the hotbar/grid, once in the armor column). Armor now has **dedicated storage**: equipping **moves** the piece out of the inventory into its armor slot (freeing the slot, ending the double-render), and unequipping returns it to a free inventory slot (refused when the inventory is full, so nothing is lost). `EquippedArmor` now holds the worn `InventorySlot` instances; the defense/durability/Mending seams read them directly (no more find-by-id, which also removes the duplicate-piece ambiguity). The save schema bumps **v11 → v12** — `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName) — with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
10	
11	### Added
12	
13	- **Equipped armor now shows on the player** in third-person (press **V**). Each worn piece renders as a procedurally-built voxel "shell" over the matching body part (helmet → head, face mask → visor, neck protection → collar, chestplate → torso + shoulder caps, leggings → upper legs, boots → feet), parented to the limb pivots so it animates with the walk/attack gait, and tinted toward the ore it's crafted from. Renderer-only (`playerModel.ts` builds the shells, `playerVisuals.ts` toggles each by what's worn) — zero new assets, no engine/save change
14	- **Grindstone**: a new crafted station (**2 cobble + 2 planks**) — the anvil's inverse, on **zero new assets** (a procedurally-painted stone-wheel block, reusing existing synth) and **no save-format or worldgen change**. Right-click to open the grindstone panel; with **enchanted** gear selected in the hotbar, **Remove enchantments** strips them all and refunds **`GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL` (5) XP per level** removed. Pure logic in `lib/game/grindstone.ts`, a new `grindstoneStrip` command, and a `GrindstoneColumn` panel; the `Grindstone` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 54), craft-only, so no worldgen baseline change
15	- **Anvil**: a new crafted station (**3 gold ore + 4 cobble**) for maintaining and consolidating gear, on **zero new assets** (a procedurally-painted dark-iron block, reusing existing synth for its clang). The save schema bumps **v10 → v11** (additive `customName`), with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
16	  - Right-click to open the anvil panel, which — like the enchanting table — acts on the **selected hotbar** tool/weapon/armor and spends XP levels. Three actions: **Combine** a duplicate (adds the two durability bars + a bonus and **merges enchantments** at the higher level, consuming the duplicate); **Repair** with the item's tier material (e.g. diamond ore for a diamond sword, cobble for a stone pickaxe) for a chunk of durability without a second copy; and **Rename** (the custom name shows everywhere the item's label does)
17	  - **Architecture**: the new `Anvil` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 53) so saved block ids never shift, and it's craft-only so no worldgen baseline changes. Pure logic lives in `lib/game/anvil.ts` (`combineSlots`, `mergeEnchantments`, `findSacrificeIndex`, `materialRepair`, `sanitizeCustomName`), driven by new `anvilCombine`/`anvilRepair`/`anvilRename` commands. The anvil station id is threaded through the **engine/UI** `craftingStation` union only (not `Recipe.station`); the panel is a new `AnvilColumn`. A per-item `customName` (additive v11 field, durable gear only, trimmed + capped) persists the rename, surfaced everywhere via a shared `displayName` helper
18	- **Mending enchantment**: a fifth enchantment for the existing enchanting table, on **zero new assets** and **no worldgen change**. Applied to any durable tool/weapon/armor (like Unbreaking), it's **binary** (max level 1) and diverts the XP you pick up into **repairing** the gear you're holding or wearing instead of banking it — `MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP` (2) durability per XP point, the held item first, then equipped armor. Implemented as one seam (`mendXp` in `enchantments.ts`) read once in `awardXp`, so XP earning, the HUD, and the sound still react to the gross pickup. The `mending` id rides the existing per-slot `enchantments`, so **no save-format bump** is needed for it
19	- **Hardcore mode**: a per-world **permadeath** toggle on the new-world form, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v9 → v10** (additive `hardcore` + `gameOver`), with **no worldgen change**
20	  - **Locked to Survival + Hard.** A hardcore world forces the game mode to Survival and the difficulty to Hard and **disables both pause-menu switchers** (immutable for the world's life), so there's no flipping to Creative or lowering the difficulty to cheat death. Its hearts render in a darker **withered** variant (a recolour of the procedural heart sprite)
21	  - **Death is permanent → spectate the dead world.** On death there is no respawn: the player flips to a **Spectator** free camera over their dead world (mobs keep roaming but can't touch them) and a **Game Over** screen offers _Spectate World_ (minimizes so you can fly around), _Back to Worlds_, or _Delete World_. The `gameOver` flag persists, so reloading a dead world resumes spectating — it can never be played again
22	  - **Architecture**: `hardcore` is a per-world boolean (`WorldMeta` + a v10 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV9toV10`), resolved first in the engine so it overrides mode/difficulty. The two lethal damage seams divert to a new `GameEngine.triggerGameOver()` (sets `gameOver`, switches to spectator, leaves `isDead` cleared so the respawn screen never shows); `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` no-op under hardcore (the death transition sets the mode directly); the shell force-saves on the `gameOver` event. New `GameOverScreen` component + a `GameShell` delete-world path
23	- **Difficulty**: the game gains Minecraft's difficulty axis — **Peaceful**, **Easy**, **Normal**, and **Hard** — orthogonal to the game mode, picked at world creation and switchable any time from the pause menu, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v8 → v9** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
24	  - **Peaceful**: no hostile mobs spawn (and switching to Peaceful instantly despawns every hostile already around — a safe panic button, the boss included), health regenerates **twice as fast**, and an empty hunger bar never hurts you — full survival minus the danger, distinct from Creative
25	  - **Easy / Normal / Hard** scale two things together: **mob hit damage** (×0.5 / ×1 / ×1.5, applied at the strike — the per-mob templates are never mutated) and **hostile spawning** (cadence + the concurrent cap, ×16 → 8 / 16 / 24)
26	  - **Starvation** (new): an empty hunger bar now has a consequence — half a heart every few seconds, down to a difficulty-scaled floor. Easy stops at 5 hearts, Normal at half a heart, and **Hard can starve you to death**; Peaceful never starves. (This changes existing **Normal** worlds: previously a fully-empty hunger bar did nothing.)
27	  - **Architecture**: a new `lib/game/difficulties.ts` holds the `Difficulty` union plus **accessor functions** (`hostilesSpawn`, `mobDamageMultiplier`, `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`, `hostileCapScale`, `regenIntervalScale`, `starves`/`starvationFloorHp`) that each system reads, mirroring the game-mode predicate pattern. Difficulty rides the same per-world plumbing as `gameMode` (`WorldMeta` + a v9 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV8toV9`); the spawn gate keys **only** on difficulty and the damage/threat gate **only** on game mode, so the two axes stay independent (Peaceful stops spawns even in Creative; Creative is invulnerable even on Hard). New `setDifficulty` command (`GameEngine.switchDifficulty`); new `STARVATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS`/`STARVATION_HP` tunables
28	- **Game modes**: the game gains Minecraft's four ways to play — **Survival** (the original), **Creative**, **Adventure**, and **Spectator** — as a single per-player axis you pick at world creation and can switch any time from the pause menu, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v7 → v8** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
29	  - **Creative**: fly (double-tap **Space**, then Space/crouch to rise/descend), take no damage and never hunger, break any block instantly, and place blocks without consuming them. The recipe book is replaced by a searchable **palette of every item** — click one to pull a stack into your inventory. The survival HUD bars hide
30	  - **Adventure**: survival in every respect (damage, hunger, mobs, combat, doors/chests/trading) **except you can't break or place blocks**, so a built world stays intact
31	  - **Spectator**: a free camera — fly through terrain (noclip), invisible and invulnerable, with no interaction at all; hostiles ignore you entirely and the HUD/hotbar hide
32	  - **Switching** modes mid-game (pause menu) refills your bars and clears any pending hazard damage, sets flight to match the mode, and lifts you out of a wall when leaving Spectator — so it's always safe to flip between them
33	  - **Architecture**: a new `lib/game/gameModes.ts` holds the `GameMode` union plus **intent predicates** (`takesDamage`, `canEditBlocks`, `freeBuild`, `canInteract`, `canFly`, `isNoclip`, `usesInventory`, `mobsThreaten`) that each system gates on, rather than comparing the raw id — so the four modes share one set of seams (the damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts`, the block edits in `mining.ts`, aggro in `mobAI.ts`, flight/noclip in `playerMotion.ts`). `gameMode` rides the existing per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` + a v8 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV7toV8`); unlike `worldType` it's the _current_, switchable value, and the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. New `setGameMode`/`toggleFlight`/`creativeGiveItem` commands; new `FLY_SPEED`/`FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` tunables
34	
35	### Changed
36	
37	- **Pause menu reorganized into tabs**: the Esc menu had grown into one long scrolling column (action buttons, the game-mode grid, volume sliders, the skin picker, and a 12-row controls list). It's now split into **Game** (save / load / reset / quit + game mode), **Options** (sound + appearance), and **Controls** (the key reference), with **Back to Game** pinned on top. Pure presentation — no save-format, worldgen, or behavior change (`components/game/PauseMenu.tsx`).
38	
39	## [0.10.0] - 2026-06-21

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

- **Equipped armor no longer occupies a hotbar/inventory slot.** Armor was equipped _by reference_ — the worn piece stayed in the inventory and kept occupying its slot (and rendered twice: once in the hotbar/grid, once in the armor column). Armor now has **dedicated storage**: equipping **moves** the piece out of the inventory into its armor slot (freeing the slot, ending the double-render), and unequipping returns it to a free inventory slot (refused when the inventory is full, so nothing is lost). `EquippedArmor` now holds the worn `InventorySlot` instances; the defense/durability/Mending seams read them directly (no more find-by-id, which also removes the duplicate-piece ambiguity). The save schema bumps **v11 → v12** — `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName) — with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)

### Added

- **Equipped armor now shows on the player** in third-person (press **V**). Each worn piece renders as a procedurally-built voxel "shell" over the matching body part (helmet → head, face mask → visor, neck protection → collar, chestplate → torso + shoulder caps, leggings → upper legs, boots → feet), parented to the limb pivots so it animates with the walk/attack gait, and tinted toward the ore it's crafted from. Renderer-only (`playerModel.ts` builds the shells, `playerVisuals.ts` toggles each by what's worn) — zero new assets, no engine/save change
- **Grindstone**: a new crafted station (**2 cobble + 2 planks**) — the anvil's inverse, on **zero new assets** (a procedurally-painted stone-wheel block, reusing existing synth) and **no save-format or worldgen change**. Right-click to open the grindstone panel; with **enchanted** gear selected in the hotbar, **Remove enchantments** strips them all and refunds **`GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL` (5) XP per level** removed. Pure logic in `lib/game/grindstone.ts`, a new `grindstoneStrip` command, and a `GrindstoneColumn` panel; the `Grindstone` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 54), craft-only, so no worldgen baseline change
- **Anvil**: a new crafted station (**3 gold ore + 4 cobble**) for maintaining and consolidating gear, on **zero new assets** (a procedurally-painted dark-iron block, reusing existing synth for its clang). The save schema bumps **v10 → v11** (additive `customName`), with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
  - Right-click to open the anvil panel, which — like the enchanting table — acts on the **selected hotbar** tool/weapon/armor and spends XP levels. Three actions: **Combine** a duplicate (adds the two durability bars + a bonus and **merges enchantments** at the higher level, consuming the duplicate); **Repair** with the item's tier material (e.g. diamond ore for a diamond sword, cobble for a stone pickaxe) for a chunk of durability without a second copy; and **Rename** (the custom name shows everywhere the item's label does)
  - **Architecture**: the new `Anvil` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 53) so saved block ids never shift, and it's craft-only so no worldgen baseline changes. Pure logic lives in `lib/game/anvil.ts` (`combineSlots`, `mergeEnchantments`, `findSacrificeIndex`, `materialRepair`, `sanitizeCustomName`), driven by new `anvilCombine`/`anvilRepair`/`anvilRename` commands. The anvil station id is threaded through the **engine/UI** `craftingStation` union only (not `Recipe.station`); the panel is a new `AnvilColumn`. A per-item `customName` (additive v11 field, durable gear only, trimmed + capped) persists the rename, surfaced everywhere via a shared `displayName` helper
- **Mending enchantment**: a fifth enchantment for the existing enchanting table, on **zero new assets** and **no worldgen change**. Applied to any durable tool/weapon/armor (like Unbreaking), it's **binary** (max level 1) and diverts the XP you pick up into **repairing** the gear you're holding or wearing instead of banking it — `MENDING_REPAIR_PER_XP` (2) durability per XP point, the held item first, then equipped armor. Implemented as one seam (`mendXp` in `enchantments.ts`) read once in `awardXp`, so XP earning, the HUD, and the sound still react to the gross pickup. The `mending` id rides the existing per-slot `enchantments`, so **no save-format bump** is needed for it
- **Hardcore mode**: a per-world **permadeath** toggle on the new-world form, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v9 → v10** (additive `hardcore` + `gameOver`), with **no worldgen change**
  - **Locked to Survival + Hard.** A hardcore world forces the game mode to Survival and the difficulty to Hard and **disables both pause-menu switchers** (immutable for the world's life), so there's no flipping to Creative or lowering the difficulty to cheat death. Its hearts render in a darker **withered** variant (a recolour of the procedural heart sprite)
  - **Death is permanent → spectate the dead world.** On death there is no respawn: the player flips to a **Spectator** free camera over their dead world (mobs keep roaming but can't touch them) and a **Game Over** screen offers _Spectate World_ (minimizes so you can fly around), _Back to Worlds_, or _Delete World_. The `gameOver` flag persists, so reloading a dead world resumes spectating — it can never be played again
  - **Architecture**: `hardcore` is a per-world boolean (`WorldMeta` + a v10 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV9toV10`), resolved first in the engine so it overrides mode/difficulty. The two lethal damage seams divert to a new `GameEngine.triggerGameOver()` (sets `gameOver`, switches to spectator, leaves `isDead` cleared so the respawn screen never shows); `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` no-op under hardcore (the death transition sets the mode directly); the shell force-saves on the `gameOver` event. New `GameOverScreen` component + a `GameShell` delete-world path
- **Difficulty**: the game gains Minecraft's difficulty axis — **Peaceful**, **Easy**, **Normal**, and **Hard** — orthogonal to the game mode, picked at world creation and switchable any time from the pause menu, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v8 → v9** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
  - **Peaceful**: no hostile mobs spawn (and switching to Peaceful instantly despawns every hostile already around — a safe panic button, the boss included), health regenerates **twice as fast**, and an empty hunger bar never hurts you — full survival minus the danger, distinct from Creative
  - **Easy / Normal / Hard** scale two things together: **mob hit damage** (×0.5 / ×1 / ×1.5, applied at the strike — the per-mob templates are never mutated) and **hostile spawning** (cadence + the concurrent cap, ×16 → 8 / 16 / 24)
  - **Starvation** (new): an empty hunger bar now has a consequence — half a heart every few seconds, down to a difficulty-scaled floor. Easy stops at 5 hearts, Normal at half a heart, and **Hard can starve you to death**; Peaceful never starves. (This changes existing **Normal** worlds: previously a fully-empty hunger bar did nothing.)
  - **Architecture**: a new `lib/game/difficulties.ts` holds the `Difficulty` union plus **accessor functions** (`hostilesSpawn`, `mobDamageMultiplier`, `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`, `hostileCapScale`, `regenIntervalScale`, `starves`/`starvationFloorHp`) that each system reads, mirroring the game-mode predicate pattern. Difficulty rides the same per-world plumbing as `gameMode` (`WorldMeta` + a v9 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV8toV9`); the spawn gate keys **only** on difficulty and the damage/threat gate **only** on game mode, so the two axes stay independent (Peaceful stops spawns even in Creative; Creative is invulnerable even on Hard). New `setDifficulty` command (`GameEngine.switchDifficulty`); new `STARVATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS`/`STARVATION_HP` tunables
- **Game modes**: the game gains Minecraft's four ways to play — **Survival** (the original), **Creative**, **Adventure**, and **Spectator** — as a single per-player axis you pick at world creation and can switch any time from the pause menu, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v7 → v8** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
  - **Creative**: fly (double-tap **Space**, then Space/crouch to rise/descend), take no damage and never hunger, break any block instantly, and place blocks without consuming them. The recipe book is replaced by a searchable **palette of every item** — click one to pull a stack into your inventory. The survival HUD bars hide
  - **Adventure**: survival in every respect (damage, hunger, mobs, combat, doors/chests/trading) **except you can't break or place blocks**, so a built world stays intact
  - **Spectator**: a free camera — fly through terrain (noclip), invisible and invulnerable, with no interaction at all; hostiles ignore you entirely and the HUD/hotbar hide
  - **Switching** modes mid-game (pause menu) refills your bars and clears any pending hazard damage, sets flight to match the mode, and lifts you out of a wall when leaving Spectator — so it's always safe to flip between them
  - **Architecture**: a new `lib/game/gameModes.ts` holds the `GameMode` union plus **intent predicates** (`takesDamage`, `canEditBlocks`, `freeBuild`, `canInteract`, `canFly`, `isNoclip`, `usesInventory`, `mobsThreaten`) that each system gates on, rather than comparing the raw id — so the four modes share one set of seams (the damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts`, the block edits in `mining.ts`, aggro in `mobAI.ts`, flight/noclip in `playerMotion.ts`). `gameMode` rides the existing per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` + a v8 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV7toV8`); unlike `worldType` it's the _current_, switchable value, and the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. New `setGameMode`/`toggleFlight`/`creativeGiveItem` commands; new `FLY_SPEED`/`FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` tunables

### Changed

- **Pause menu reorganized into tabs**: the Esc menu had grown into one long scrolling column (action buttons, the game-mode grid, volume sliders, the skin picker, and a 12-row controls list). It's now split into **Game** (save / load / reset / quit + game mode), **Options** (sound + appearance), and **Controls** (the key reference), with **Back to Game** pinned on top. Pure presentation — no save-format, worldgen, or behavior change (`components/game/PauseMenu.tsx`).

## [0.10.0] - 2026-06-21

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(enchant): add Power and Punch for bows

The enchanting system shipped with five enchantments but nothing for the
bow, leaving ranged combat without a progression path. Add two bow
enchantments — Power (+arrow damage) and Punch (+arrow knockback) — read
off the held bow at the single tryFireBow seam, matching the existing
one-reader-per-seam discipline.

Because the bow is kind "weapon" (like swords), a plain kind gate would
wrongly offer these on swords. Add an optional itemIds allow-list to
EnchantmentDef; canEnchant honors it on top of the kind check, binding
Power/Punch to the bow only. This is the one new registry capability.

Their ids ride the existing per-slot enchantments field (added to the
compile-enforced VALID_ENCHANT_IDS), so there is no save-format bump and
WORLDGEN_VERSION stays 8 — the same additive-id pattern as Mending.
EOF
git log --oneline -1

- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.

- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.

- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.

+- **Unreleased (no save bump)** — new enchantments (**Power**, **Punch**, **Knockback**, **Looting**, **Fortune**, **Feather Falling**) ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` field; their ids are added to the save validator's known-id set (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS`, a compile-enforced `Record<EnchantmentId, true>`). No new field, no new `BlockId`, no worldgen change — the save schema stays **v12** and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** (the same additive-id pattern as Mending). Older builds silently drop unknown ids on load.

- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.

- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.

- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.

- **Weapon enchantments — Knockback & Looting**: two new enchantments for any weapon, on **zero new assets** and **no save-format or worldgen change**. **Knockback** adds `KNOCKBACK_PER_LEVEL` (0.4) to the melee shove per level (the base shove is now the named `MELEE_KNOCKBACK_IMPULSE` (0.75), no longer a magic number), read off the held weapon at the `tryAttackMob` seam. **Looting** rolls up to `LOOTING_BONUS_PER_LEVEL` (1) extra of each mob drop per level off the killing weapon, in `rollMobDrops`. Both ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` (added to `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS`), so no save bump

- **Bow enchantments — Power & Punch**: two new enchantments for the existing enchanting table, on **zero new assets** and **no save-format or worldgen change**. **Power** adds `POWER_DAMAGE_PER_LEVEL` (2) arrow damage per level and **Punch** adds `PUNCH_KNOCKBACK_PER_LEVEL` (0.25) arrow knockback per level, both read off the held bow at the single `tryFireBow` seam. They're **bow-only**: `EnchantmentDef` gains an optional `itemIds` allow-list (`canEnchant` honors it on top of the item-kind gate), so these don't appear on swords (which are also `weapon`). Their ids ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` (added to `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS`), so no save bump (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)

- **Equipped armor now shows on the player** in third-person (press **V**). Each worn piece renders as a procedurally-built voxel "shell" over the matching body part (helmet → head, face mask → visor, neck protection → collar, chestplate → torso + shoulder caps, leggings → upper legs, boots → feet), parented to the limb pivots so it animates with the walk/attack gait, and tinted toward the ore it's crafted from. Renderer-only (`playerModel.ts` builds the shells, `playerVisuals.ts` toggles each by what's worn) — zero new assets, no engine/save change

1	# Gameplay Reference
2	
3	Scannable tables for everything in the game: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item
4	stats. For how it all fits together, read the [player manual](manual.md).
5	
6	> **The code is the source of truth.** These tables are a convenience snapshot of
7	> `lib/game/recipes.ts`, `lib/game/items.ts`, `lib/world/blocks.ts`,
8	> `lib/game/mobs.ts`, and `lib/game/mobLoot.ts`. If a number here disagrees with
9	> the game, the code wins — and this page needs an update.
10	
11	## Game modes
12	
13	Chosen at world creation and switchable any time from the pause menu; saved with
14	the world and independent of the world type. Source: `lib/game/gameModes.ts` (the
15	`GameMode` union + predicates each system gates on).
16	
17	| Mode      | Damage / hunger | Break / place blocks   | Flight       | Interact (combat, doors, eat) | Mobs       | Inventory         |
18	| --------- | --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- |
19	| Survival  | Yes             | Yes                    | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
20	| Creative  | No (invincible) | Instant, free (no use) | Yes          | Yes                           | Ignore you | All-items palette |
21	| Adventure | Yes             | **No**                 | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
22	| Spectator | No (invincible) | No                     | Yes (noclip) | **No**                        | Ignore you | Hidden            |
23	
24	## Difficulty
25	
26	A separate axis from the game mode — also chosen at world creation, switchable from
27	the pause menu, and saved with the world. Sets how hard survival is. Source:
28	`lib/game/difficulties.ts` (the `Difficulty` union + accessors each system reads).
29	
30	| Level    | Hostiles spawn             | Mob damage | Spawn rate / cap  | Starvation            |
31	| -------- | -------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- | --------------------- |
32	| Peaceful | No (and despawns existing) | —          | none / 0          | Never (regen ×2 fast) |
33	| Easy     | Yes                        | ×0.5       | slower / cap 8    | Stops at 5 hearts     |
34	| Normal   | Yes                        | ×1.0       | baseline / cap 16 | Stops at ½ heart      |
35	| Hard     | Yes                        | ×1.5       | faster / cap 24   | Kills you             |
36	
37	## Hardcore
38	
39	A per-world toggle (immutable, chosen at creation) for permadeath. Forces **Survival**
40	mode and **Hard** difficulty and locks both switchers. On death the run ends: the
41	world flips to a spectator "dead world" with a Game Over screen (Spectate / Back to
42	Worlds / Delete World), and the dead state persists across reloads. Hearts render in
43	a withered dark-red variant. Source: the `hardcore`/`gameOver` flags in
44	`lib/game/types.ts` + `GameEngine.triggerGameOver`.
45	
46	## World types
47	
48	Chosen when you create a world (alongside the name and seed) and fixed for its
49	life. All four share the same five biomes — they reshape terrain, not the biome
50	mix. Source: `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` + `terrainConfigFor` in `lib/world/generation.ts`.
51	
52	| Type      | Terrain                                                                                     |
53	| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
54	| Default   | Balanced terrain with every biome — the original generator                                  |
55	| Superflat | Level ground at a fixed height; a builder's canvas (caves and ores still generate below)    |
56	| Amplified | Exaggerated relief — towering peaks and deep valleys                                        |
57	| Islands   | A raised sea breaks the land into scattered, gently sloped islands with deep ocean channels |
58	
59	## Recipes
60	
61	**68 crafting recipes** (plus **10 villager trades**, listed under [Trading](#trading)).
62	All use the always-available crafting grid except the nine **furnace** smelting
63	recipes (need an open furnace) and the five **brewing** recipes (need an open
64	[brewing stand](#brewing--potions)).
65	
66	In-game, the recipe book groups recipes into the sections below (Tools, Weapons,
67	Armor, Building, Food, Materials, then Smelting, Brewing, and Trades), listing the
68	recipes you can currently afford first within each section. Hovering a recipe you
69	can't afford shows each ingredient as have / need plus a "how to obtain it" hint
70	for the missing ones (derived from the loot/recipe tables in `itemSources.ts`).

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(enchant): add Fortune and Feather Falling

Tools had no yield enchantment and there was nothing to soften falls.
Add Fortune (tools) — more ore per mine — and Feather Falling (boots) —
less fall damage.

Fortune threads an optional level into rollBlockDrops (default 0 keeps
every existing caller and test unchanged) and rolls a bonus only for the
ore blocks, read off the mining tool in addBlockDrop. Feather Falling is
boots-only via the itemIds allow-list and reduces the raw fall damage in
tickPlayerMotion (before armor mitigation), capped so a tampered level
can't zero out fall damage. The melee base shove is named
MELEE_KNOCKBACK_IMPULSE; the cap is FEATHER_FALLING_MAX_REDUCTION.

Both ids ride the existing per-slot enchantments field (added to the
compile-enforced VALID_ENCHANT_IDS), so no save bump and WORLDGEN_VERSION
stays 8.
EOF
git log --oneline -3

## Status effects & potions

`EFFECT_SPEED_DURATION`/`EFFECT_SPEED_MULTIPLIER`,
`EFFECT_STRENGTH_DURATION`/`EFFECT_STRENGTH_BONUS`,
`EFFECT_REGEN_DURATION`/`EFFECT_REGEN_INTERVAL`/`EFFECT_REGEN_HP`,
`EFFECT_FIRE_RESIST_DURATION`, `EFFECT_WATER_BREATHING_DURATION`,
`POISON_DURATION`/`POISON_INTERVAL`/`POISON_HP`/`POISON_FLOOR_HP`,
`ROTTEN_FLESH_POISON_CHANCE`.

Read by `systems/statusEffects.ts` (and the seams it feeds: `playerMotion.ts`
for speed, the melee dispatch in `GameEngine.ts` for strength, and the gated
`tickLavaExposure`/`tickOxygen` for fire-resist/water-breathing). The
`*_DURATION` values are how long a drunk potion lasts (default Minecraft-ish:
buffs 3:00, Regeneration 0:45). **Strength** adds `EFFECT_STRENGTH_BONUS` (3) flat
melee damage; **Speed** multiplies movement by `EFFECT_SPEED_MULTIPLIER` (1.2);
**Regeneration** heals `EFFECT_REGEN_HP` (1) every `EFFECT_REGEN_INTERVAL` (1.5 s)
on its **own** accumulator, ignoring the hunger gate. **Poison** ticks `POISON_HP`
(1) every `POISON_INTERVAL` (1.25 s) but floors at `POISON_FLOOR_HP` (1) so it can
never kill; eating rotten flesh inflicts it with probability
`ROTTEN_FLESH_POISON_CHANCE` (0.8) for `POISON_DURATION` (8 s). Brewing reagent
costs are balanced in `recipes.ts`, not here. Lengthen the buffs or cut the poison
odds to make the system gentler; the reagent map is the economic dial.

Their ids are added to the save validators' known-id sets (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` / `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`, both compile-enforced `Record<…, true>`). No new field, no new `BlockId`, no worldgen change — the save schema stays **v12** and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** (the same additive-id pattern as Mending). Older builds silently drop unknown ids on load.

- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.

- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.

- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.

attachment.snippet:
1	# Gameplay Reference
2	
3	Scannable tables for everything in the game: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item
4	stats. For how it all fits together, read the [player manual](manual.md).
5	
6	> **The code is the source of truth.** These tables are a convenience snapshot of
7	> `lib/game/recipes.ts`, `lib/game/items.ts`, `lib/world/blocks.ts`,
8	> `lib/game/mobs.ts`, and `lib/game/mobLoot.ts`. If a number here disagrees with
9	> the game, the code wins — and this page needs an update.
10	
11	## Game modes
12	
13	Chosen at world creation and switchable any time from the pause menu; saved with
14	the world and independent of the world type. Source: `lib/game/gameModes.ts` (the
15	`GameMode` union + predicates each system gates on).
16	
17	| Mode      | Damage / hunger | Break / place blocks   | Flight       | Interact (combat, doors, eat) | Mobs       | Inventory         |
18	| --------- | --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- |
19	| Survival  | Yes             | Yes                    | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
20	| Creative  | No (invincible) | Instant, free (no use) | Yes          | Yes                           | Ignore you | All-items palette |
21	| Adventure | Yes             | **No**                 | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
22	| Spectator | No (invincible) | No                     | Yes (noclip) | **No**                        | Ignore you | Hidden            |
23	
24	## Difficulty
25	
26	A separate axis from the game mode — also chosen at world creation, switchable from
27	the pause menu, and saved with the world. Sets how hard survival is. Source:
28	`lib/game/difficulties.ts` (the `Difficulty` union + accessors each system reads).
29	
30	| Level    | Hostiles spawn             | Mob damage | Spawn rate / cap  | Starvation            |
31	| -------- | -------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- | --------------------- |
32	| Peaceful | No (and despawns existing) | —          | none / 0          | Never (regen ×2 fast) |
33	| Easy     | Yes                        | ×0.5       | slower / cap 8    | Stops at 5 hearts     |
34	| Normal   | Yes                        | ×1.0       | baseline / cap 16 | Stops at ½ heart      |
35	| Hard     | Yes                        | ×1.5       | faster / cap 24   | Kills you             |
36	
37	## Hardcore
38	
39	A per-world toggle (immutable, chosen at creation) for permadeath. Forces **Survival**
40	mode and **Hard** difficulty and locks both switchers. On death the run ends: the
41	world flips to a spectator "dead world" with a Game Over screen (Spectate / Back to
42	Worlds / Delete World), and the dead state persists across reloads. Hearts render in
43	a withered dark-red variant. Source: the `hardcore`/`gameOver` flags in
44	`lib/game/types.ts` + `GameEngine.triggerGameOver`.
45	
46	## World types
47

1	# Tuning & Balance
2	
3	Every gameplay tunable lives in one place: [`lib/game/config.ts`](../lib/game/config.ts).
4	Each constant there carries a one-line comment; this guide is the companion that
5	groups them by **what they affect**, names the **system that reads each**, and
6	flags the **balance trade-offs** and the few that are **save-sensitive**.
7	
8	To rebalance, edit `config.ts` — not the systems. Item-level numbers (a pickaxe's
9	power, a sword's damage, a food's hunger) are **not** here; they live with the
10	content in [`items.ts`](../lib/game/items.ts) (see the [reference](reference.md)).
11	Worldgen constants live in the frozen `GEN` object in
12	[`generation.ts`](../lib/world/generation.ts) and are pinned by hash tests — see
13	[testing.md](testing.md).
14	
15	## Player feel — physics & movement
16	
17	`GRAVITY`, `JUMP_VELOCITY`, `WALK_SPEED`, `SPRINT_SPEED`, `CROUCH_SPEED`,
18	`PLAYER_HEIGHT`, `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`, `EYE_HEIGHT`, `WORLD_BORDER_PADDING`.
19	
20	Read by `systems/playerMotion.ts`. These set the moment-to-moment feel.
21	`JUMP_VELOCITY` vs `GRAVITY` together fix jump height (currently a ~1-block hop);
22	raise gravity for a snappier, heavier fall. `SPRINT_SPEED` is deliberately far
23	above `WALK_SPEED` so sprinting feels like a meaningful choice (and it's what burns
24	hunger fastest). `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`/`PLAYER_HEIGHT` are also the collision box, so
25	changing them affects which gaps the player fits through.
26	
27	## Game modes — flight
28	
29	`FLY_SPEED`, `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS`.
30	
31	Used by the flight path in `systems/playerMotion.ts` and the double-tap detector
32	in `input/inputController.ts`. `FLY_SPEED` is the vertical climb/descend speed
33	while flying (Creative and Spectator); horizontal speed still comes from
34	`WALK_SPEED`/`SPRINT_SPEED`. `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` is how close two
35	`Space` presses must be to toggle flight — raise it if a double-tap feels hard to
36	trigger, lower it if flight toggles by accident while bunny-hopping. (The modes
37	themselves and their gates live in `lib/game/gameModes.ts`, not `config.ts`.)
38	
39	## Survival pressure — the main difficulty dial
40	
41	`MAX_HEARTS`, `MAX_HUNGER`, `RESPAWN_SECONDS`, `HEALTH_REGEN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`,
42	`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER`, `SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER`, `SPRINT_BLOCKS_PER_HUNGER`,
43	`WALK_BLOCKS_PER_HUNGER`, `JUMPS_PER_HUNGER`, `STARVATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS`,
44	`STARVATION_HP`, `WATER_DAMAGE_DELAY_SECONDS`, `WATER_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`,
45	`WATER_DAMAGE_HP`.
46	
47	Read by `systems/playerStats.ts` (drain + regen) and `systems/playerLife.ts`
48	(respawn). This group is where "how hard is it to stay alive" is set. The
49	`*_PER_HUNGER` budgets control how fast activity drains food — lower numbers = more
50	eating. The two gates are the key feedback loop: you must stay above
51	`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER` (12) to heal and above `SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER` (6) to sprint, so
52	hunger pressure indirectly throttles both combat recovery and escape speed. Keep
53	`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER > SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER` so there's a "can run but can't heal" band.
54	Water exposure is continuous body-midpoint immersion: leaving water resets both
55	timers. After `WATER_DAMAGE_DELAY_SECONDS` (60), environmental damage bypasses
56	armor every `WATER_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (1) for `WATER_DAMAGE_HP` (3 HP = 1.5
57	hearts). These counters are transient and reset on reload/respawn.
58	**Starvation** is the consequence of a fully-empty hunger bar: once `hunger` hits
59	0, `STARVATION_HP` (1 HP) is lost every `STARVATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (4) down to a
60	**difficulty-scaled floor** (see below) — these two constants are the cadence; the
61	floor is the per-level dial.
62	
63	## Difficulty — Peaceful / Easy / Normal / Hard
64	
65	The per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts` (accessor functions,
66	not `config.ts` constants — the _base_ values they bend stay in `config.ts`). It is
67	an axis orthogonal to game mode, picked at world creation and switchable in the
68	pause menu; the spawn directors and mob AI read `state.difficulty` every tick.
69	
70	| Dial (accessor)                       | Peaceful | Easy | Normal | Hard |
71	| ------------------------------------- | -------- | ---- | ------ | ---- |
72	| `hostilesSpawn`                       | no       | yes  | yes    | yes  |
73	| `mobDamageMultiplier` (×hit)          | —        | 0.5  | 1      | 1.5  |
74	| `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`           | —        | 1.5  | 1      | 0.6  |
75	| `hostileCapScale` (×`HOSTILE_CAP` 16) | 0        | 8    | 16     | 24   |
76	| `regenIntervalScale` (×regen)         | 0.5      | 1    | 1      | 1    |
77	| `starvationFloorHp` (HP floor)        | never    | 10   | 1      | 0    |
78	
79	Read by `systems/spawnDirector.ts` (the spawn gate + cadence/cap scales),
80	`systems/mobAI.ts` (the per-hit damage scale, applied at the strike — templates are
81	never mutated), and `systems/playerStats.ts` (faster Peaceful regen + the
82	starvation floor). **Peaceful** also despawns existing hostiles the moment you
83	switch to it (`GameEngine.switchDifficulty`). Note these dials are independent of
84	game mode: Peaceful stops hostile _spawns_ regardless of mode, while damage/threat
85	still gate on the mode (Creative is invulnerable at any difficulty). The **Hardcore**
86	flag (a per-world boolean, not a tunable) forces this dial to Hard and locks it — see
87	`docs/architecture.md` for the permadeath/game-over flow.
88	
89	## Cave hazards — lava & drowning
90	
91	`LAVA_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, `LAVA_DAMAGE_HP`, `LAVA_BURN_SECONDS`,
92	`MAX_OXYGEN`, `OXYGEN_HOLD_SECONDS`, `OXYGEN_REFILL_SECONDS`,
93	`OXYGEN_DROWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, `OXYGEN_DROWN_HP`.
94	
95	Read by `systems/playerStats.ts` (`tickLavaExposure`, `tickOxygen`), both on the
96	armor-bypassing damage path. **Lava** burns the instant you touch it (no grace
97	period, unlike water) for `LAVA_DAMAGE_HP` (6 = 3 hearts) every
98	`LAVA_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (0.5) and keeps burning `LAVA_BURN_SECONDS` (3)
99	after you escape — the deep-cave death trap. Lava is solid, so contact is checked
100	underfoot/at the body, not by immersion. **Drowning** keys on the head: the
101	bubble meter drains over `OXYGEN_HOLD_SECONDS` (15) while the eye cell is
102	underwater, then deals `OXYGEN_DROWN_HP` (2) every `OXYGEN_DROWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`
103	(1); surfacing refills it over `OXYGEN_REFILL_SECONDS` (1.5). This is separate
104	from the body-keyed 60 s water-exposure timer above — wading chest-deep never
105	drowns you. All these counters are transient (reset on reload/respawn).
106	
107	Lighting itself has no `config.ts` tunables: the per-voxel light propagation is
108	in [`lib/world/lighting.ts`](../lib/world/lighting.ts) (block opacity/emission and
109	the 0–15 levels), and the cave-darkness floor + torch tint are shader constants in
110	[`GameRenderer.ts`](../lib/game/render/GameRenderer.ts) (`SKY_LIGHT_FLOOR`,
111	`TORCH_TINT`).
112	
113	## Status effects & potions
114	
115	`EFFECT_SPEED_DURATION`/`EFFECT_SPEED_MULTIPLIER`,
116	`EFFECT_STRENGTH_DURATION`/`EFFECT_STRENGTH_BONUS`,
117	`EFFECT_REGEN_DURATION`/`EFFECT_REGEN_INTERVAL`/`EFFECT_REGEN_HP`,
118	`EFFECT_FIRE_RESIST_DURATION`, `EFFECT_WATER_BREATHING_DURATION`,
119	`EFFECT_HASTE_DURATION`/`EFFECT_HASTE_MULTIPLIER`,
120	`EFFECT_RESISTANCE_DURATION`/`EFFECT_RESISTANCE_MULTIPLIER`,
121	`EFFECT_JUMP_BOOST_DURATION`/`EFFECT_JUMP_BOOST_VELOCITY`,
122	`POISON_DURATION`/`POISON_INTERVAL`/`POISON_HP`/`POISON_FLOOR_HP`,
123	`ROTTEN_FLESH_POISON_CHANCE`.
124	
125	Read by `systems/statusEffects.ts` (and the seams it feeds: `playerMotion.ts`
126	for speed and jump-boost, the melee dispatch in `GameEngine.ts` for strength,
127	`mining.ts` for haste, `playerLife.ts` for resistance, and the gated
128	`tickLavaExposure`/`tickOxygen` for fire-resist/water-breathing). The
129	`*_DURATION` values are how long a drunk potion lasts (default Minecraft-ish:
130	buffs 3:00, Regeneration 0:45). **Strength** adds `EFFECT_STRENGTH_BONUS` (3) flat
131	melee damage; **Speed** multiplies movement by `EFFECT_SPEED_MULTIPLIER` (1.2);
132	**Haste** multiplies mining speed by `EFFECT_HASTE_MULTIPLIER` (1.4);

feat(brewing): add Haste, Resistance, and Jump Boost potions

The potion system had five buffs and no mining, defensive, or mobility
option. Add three brewable potions — Haste (faster mining), Resistance
(less combat damage), and Leaping/Jump Boost (higher jumps) — each an
engine-only effect read at one seam.

Haste multiplies mining progress in tickMining; Resistance scales the
post-armor combat damage in applyDamageWithArmor only, leaving the
unmitigated lava/void/poison paths alone (asserted in tests); Jump Boost
adds to the jump launch velocity in tickPlayerMotion, tuned to stay under
the fall-damage threshold so leaping never self-damages. Each is brewed
from an existing reagent, gets a procedurally-painted HUD icon and bottle
sprite (no new assets, no renderer change), and rides the existing
top-level effects field (added to the compile-enforced VALID_EFFECT_IDS),
so no save bump and WORLDGEN_VERSION stays 8.
EOF

content.subject: Commit 1: Power + Punch enchantments (bow) + itemIds allow-list
content.description: Add optional itemIds to EnchantmentDef + canEnchant support; add Power (bow damage) and Punch (bow knockback) enchantments wired into tryFireBow; config tunables; save validator entries; docs + tests + CHANGELOG.

content.subject: Commit 2: Knockback + Looting enchantments (weapons)
content.description: Add Knockback (tryAttackMob impulse param) and Looting (rollMobDrops count) enchantments; config; save validator; docs + tests + CHANGELOG.

content.subject: Commit 3: Fortune + Feather Falling enchantments
content.description: Add Fortune (ore-gated rollBlockDrops multiplier) and Feather Falling (playerMotion fall-damage reducer); config; save validator; docs + tests + CHANGELOG.

content.subject: Commit 4: Haste + Resistance + Jump Boost potions
content.description: Add 3 status effects with one-seam readers (mining/playerLife/playerMotion), potion items, brewing recipes, HUD icons, save validator; docs + tests + CHANGELOG.

content.subject: Verify gate + open PR
content.description: Run full CI verify gate (lint, typecheck, format:check, test, build); confirm docs/CHANGELOG cover everything; open PR against hutusi/main when user authorizes.

content.text:
The "Deepen progression" feature is complete on branch `feat/deepen-progression` — **5 commits, 31 files, +744/−80**, with the full CI gate green.

## What shipped

**6 new enchantments** (all one-seam additions, gated correctly via the new optional `itemIds` allow-list where needed):
- **Power / Punch** — bow arrow damage / knockback (bow-only)
- **Knockback / Looting** — melee shove / bonus mob drops (any weapon)
- **Fortune** — extra ore on mining (tools, ore-blocks only)
- **Feather Falling** — softer landings (boots-only)

**3 new potions / status effects** (engine-only, HUD icons + bottle sprites, no renderer changes):
- **Haste** (×1.4 mining), **Resistance** (×0.8 combat damage only — lava/void/poison untouched), **Leaping** (higher jumps, tuned under the fall-damage threshold)

**Key invariants held:** zero new binary assets, **no save-format bump** (new ids ride the existing `enchantments`/`effects` fields, validated by the compile-enforced `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS`/`VALID_EFFECT_IDS` totality maps), and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8**.

## Verification (all green)
- `lint` · `typecheck` · `format:check` · **853 unit/integration/component tests** · `build`
- **17 Playwright e2e** smoke tests
- New tests cover every seam: enchant readers + `itemIds` gating, Looting/Fortune rolls, Knockback impulse, Feather Falling/Haste/Jump Boost through the engine, Resistance's combat-only scope, and additive save round-trips.
- Docs updated with each change: `reference.md`, `manual.md`, `tuning.md`, `save-format.md`, `adding-content.md`, `testing.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Two notes
- **Not pushed / no PR opened** — per your repo policy (pushing & PRs are user-authorized) and your standing "review fixes: no push" preference. Say the word and I'll push and open the PR against `hutusi/main`.
- **One optional manual check:** the new effect HUD icons (gold star / steel shield / green up-arrow) and the three potion bottle tints are procedurally drawn — unit tests confirm they render as non-empty 16×16 sprites, but if you want them visually eyeballed, run `bun run dev`, brew one of each, and glance at the top-left effect readout.

Want me to push the branch and open the PR?

## Enchantments (6)

| Enchant | Applies to | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Power** | bows | +2 arrow damage / level |
| **Punch** | bows | +0.25 arrow knockback / level |
| **Knockback** | weapons | +0.4 melee shove / level |
| **Looting** | weapons | up to +1 of each mob drop / level |
| **Fortune** | tools | up to +1 ore / level (ore blocks only) |
| **Feather Falling** | boots | −15% fall damage / level (caps at −80%) |

| Potion | Reagent | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Haste** | Gold Ore | ×1.4 mining speed |
| **Resistance** | Leather | ×0.8 incoming **combat** damage (lava/void/poison untouched) |
| **Leaping** | Sliver Ore | +2 jump launch velocity (tuned under the fall-damage threshold) |

Engine-only buffs with procedurally-painted HUD icons + bottle sprites — no renderer changes.

## Where it plugs in

Each addition is a flat per-level/effect modifier read at exactly one seam: `tryFireBow` (Power/Punch), `tryAttackMob` (Knockback), `rollMobDrops` (Looting), `rollBlockDrops` (Fortune), `tickPlayerMotion` (Feather Falling + Jump Boost), `mining.ts` (Haste), `applyDamageWithArmor` (Resistance). Syncs the fork's `main` back to upstream — **58 commits** since the last sync (#9, living world & fishing). Everything is additive and backward-compatible; the save schema advances **v5 → v10** through a chain of pure version-bump migrations (`readSave` chains v1 → … → v10), so existing worlds load clean. CI is green on the fork's `main` (lint, typecheck, format, full unit suite, build, and Playwright e2e).

## What's included (oldest → newest)

- **Status effects, brewing & potions** (#28, save v5→v6) — six timed effects (Speed, Strength, Regeneration, Fire Resistance, Water Breathing, and a never-lethal Poison), a **Brewing Stand** station that reuses the recipe pipeline, and potions drunk with `F`. Each effect is read at exactly one existing seam.
- **XP & enchanting** (#29, save v6→v7) — banked XP from kills/ore/fishing (not lost on death), an **Enchanting Table** that spends XP levels on deterministic, player-chosen enchantments (Sharpness / Protection / Efficiency / Unbreaking, up to level 3). Enchantments are per-item-instance data riding the existing durability/snapshot plumbing.
- **Crafting recipe hints + 3 fixes** (#30) — unaffordable recipes show have/need per ingredient plus a "how to obtain it" hint (from a new `itemSources.ts`); plus fixes for player-position load validation, a block-atlas texture leak, and save-on-unmount.
- **Release v0.10.0** — rolls the above into a tagged release.
- **Game modes** (#31, save v7→v8) — Minecraft's four modes (**Survival / Creative / Adventure / Spectator**) as one per-player axis, picked at creation and switchable in the pause menu. Built on intent **predicates** (`takesDamage`/`canEditBlocks`/`canFly`/`isNoclip`/…) so all four share one set of seams. Creative gets an all-items palette + double-tap-Space flight.
- **Pause menu → tabs** (#32) — the Esc menu split into **Game / Options / Controls** (pure UI; no save/behavior change).
- **Difficulty** (#33, save v8→v9) — **Peaceful / Easy / Normal / Hard** as an axis orthogonal to game mode. Peaceful disables hostile spawns (and despawns existing ones) + faster regen; Easy/Normal/Hard scale mob damage and spawn cadence/cap; plus a new difficulty-scaled **hunger starvation** mechanic. Per-level numbers live as accessors in `difficulties.ts`.
- **Hardcore** (#34, save v9→v10) — a per-world **permadeath** toggle that locks Survival + Hard. On death the run ends: the player flips to a **Spectator** free-cam over their dead world with a **Game Over** screen (Spectate / Back to Worlds / Delete World); the dead state persists. Hearts render in a withered variant.

## Notes for review

- **Zero new binary assets** throughout — every sprite/texture is pixel-code, every sound is synthesized (the project's standing principle).
- **Save compatibility**: each step is an optional additive field with a pure migration; pre-feature saves restore with sensible defaults (e.g. `gameMode` → survival, `difficulty` → normal, `hardcore`/`gameOver` → false). No `WORLDGEN_VERSION` change in any of these.
- **Worth a manual gameplay pass** on the visual/interactive bits that headless tests can't fully cover: the Creative palette + flight, the brewing/enchanting panels, and especially Hardcore's death → spectator → Game Over flow.

Docs are updated alongside each feature (architecture, save-format, tuning, manual, reference, README, CHANGELOG).

content.text: `main` → `0a7695d` and tag `v0.11.0` pushed. Now opening the upstream sync PR (`hutusi:main` → `davidhu0527:main`), in the house style of the prior sync (#11), no AI-attribution:

input.command:
cd /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft
gh pr create --repo davidhu0527/monecraft --base main --head hutusi:main \
  --title "Sync fork: gear progression, equipped-armor storage & render, and more enchantments & potions (v0.11.0)" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Syncs the fork's `main` back to upstream — **20 commits** since the last sync (#11, v0.10.0), cut as **v0.11.0**. Everything is additive and backward-compatible; the save schema advances **v10 → v12** through pure version-bump migrations (`readSave` chains v1 → … → v12), so existing worlds load clean. CI is green on the fork's `main` (lint, typecheck, format, full unit suite, build, and Playwright e2e).

## What's included (oldest → newest)

- **Anvil, Grindstone & Mending** (#35, save v10→v11) — a **Mending** enchantment (binary; diverts picked-up XP to repair held/worn gear; no save bump — rides the existing per-slot `enchantments`), an **Anvil** station (repair with the item's tier material, combine duplicates merging enchantments, rename gear) and a **Grindstone** (strip enchantments, refund XP). The v11 bump adds an optional per-item `customName` (the anvil rename). Both blocks are craft-only — no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` change.
- **Equipped-armor storage & third-person render** (#36, save v11→v12) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory occupying a slot (and double-rendered). Armor now has **dedicated storage**: `equippedArmor` holds the worn pieces themselves, and `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves legacy by-id equips out of the inventory (preserving durability/enchantments/customName). Worn pieces now also render as procedural voxel **shells** on the third-person player model (renderer-only).
- **Deepen progression: more enchantments & potions** (#37, no save bump) — six new enchantments (**Power**/**Punch** for bows, **Knockback**/**Looting** for weapons, **Fortune** for tools, **Feather Falling** for boots) and three new brewed potions (**Haste**, **Resistance**, **Leaping**). `EnchantmentDef` gains an optional `itemIds` allow-list (binds Power/Punch to the bow, Feather Falling to boots); Looting applies on melee kills only. Every new enchant/effect id rides an existing validated save field (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS`/`VALID_EFFECT_IDS`), so **no save bump** — the same additive-id pattern as Mending.

## Notes for review

- **Zero new binary assets** throughout — every sprite/texture is pixel-code, every sound synthesized (the project's standing principle). The new HUD effect icons, potion bottles, and armor shells are all procedurally generated.
- **Save compatibility**: v10 → v11 → v12 are additive with pure migrations, and the deepen-progression ids are additive enum values on already-validated fields; pre-feature saves load clean and older builds drop unknown ids. **No `WORLDGEN_VERSION` change** in any of these (stays 8).
- **Worth a manual gameplay pass** on the visual/interactive bits headless tests can't fully cover: the anvil/grindstone panels, equipped armor on the third-person model, and the new HUD effect icons.

Docs are updated alongside each feature (architecture/adding-content, save-format, tuning, manual, reference, CHANGELOG).
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

---
name: roadmap-candidates
description: "Candidate next-feature directions for the voxel game — what's shipped vs still open (anvil/grindstone/mending #35 + armor-dedicated-slots/armor-visuals #36 both MERGED, save now v12, as of 2026-06-28)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e2fc6b63-8357-4ed9-b4cc-94b55fc71192
