## Status: gear progression + armor fix (2026-06-28)

**Anvil/Grindstone/Mending — `hutusi/monecraft#35` MERGED** (merge commit `1aca8fd`; merged via merge commit, `--delete-branch` removed remote+local `feat/anvil-grindstone-mending`). Adds **Mending** (5th enchant; `mendXp` seam in `enchantments.ts` read once in `awardXp` — diverts gained XP to repair held/worn gear), an **Anvil** (craft 3 gold ore + 4 cobble; combine duplicate / material repair / rename, on the selected hotbar item) and a **Grindstone** (craft 2 cobble + 2 planks; strip enchants for XP). Save **v10→v11** (additive per-item `customName`; `mendXp`/`displayName`/`REPAIR_MATERIAL_BY_ITEM` in `items.ts`; pure logic in `anvil.ts`/`grindstone.ts`). New craft-only BlockIds Anvil=53, Grindstone=54 (no `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump, stays 8). Dedicated `AnvilColumn`/`GrindstoneColumn` panels; station ids on the engine/UI `craftingStation` union only (not `Recipe.station`). CodeRabbit (only reviewer) had 9 findings — 6 applied (per-enchant save clamp so a tampered `mending:3` loads as 1, anvil rename field keyed on saved name + sanitized submit, 2 doc reconciliations, test type-safety, config-constant assertion), 3 declined-with-rationale (the EquippedArmor-by-id ambiguity = pre-existing, see #36; the `as unknown as GameState` test fixture = repo-wide pattern).

**Armor dedicated storage + armor-on-body visuals — `hutusi/monecraft#36` MERGED** (2026-06-28, merge commit `2efafa8`; merged via merge commit + `--delete-branch`; local `main` synced, branch deleted). Fixed a **pre-existing** bug (user-reported): equipped armor occupied a hotbar slot because equipping was a by-reference marker (`equippedArmor[slot]=id`) leaving the item in the inventory (double-render + by-id ambiguity). Now `EquippedArmor = Record<ArmorSlot, InventorySlot|null>` (worn instances); `toggleEquipArmor` MOVES the piece out of inventory (swap-on-occupied), new `unequipArmor` moves it back (refused when full); `equippedDefense`/`armorReduction`/`consumeEquippedArmorDurability`/`mendXp` read the record directly; `syncEquippedArmor`/`unequipMissingArmor` deleted. Save **v11→v12** (`equippedArmor` persists per-slot `SavedSlot` via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`; `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves legacy by-id equips out of `inventorySlots`). Storage fix was one atomic commit `c751cdb` (type coupling). The PR also **bundled** (user chose to add on): (a) a CodeRabbit fix — clear `pendingIndex` on armor-column unequip; (b) **armor shown on the third-person player model** (`feat(render)` `06ec681`) — `playerModel.ts` builds a procedural voxel **shell** per slot over the matching body part (helmet→head crown, face_mask→visor, neck→collar, chestplate→torso+2 shoulder caps, leggings→upper legs, boots→feet), parented to limb pivots so it animates, **ore-tinted** per slot (`ARMOR_TINT` map), hidden until worn; `playerVisuals.ts` toggles each slot by `equippedArmor[slot] != null` (new `equippedArmor` field on `PlayerVisualsState`, already flows via `GameRenderer.sync`); renderer-only, zero assets. CodeRabbit posted 1 finding (pending-slot, applied) + 1 nitpick (strengthen the multi-part-shell test, applied `afe7fb2`). Final gate green: lint/typecheck/format/**832 unit**/build + **17 e2e**. NOT released. **Manual third-person pass still recommended** — the armor shells' box sizes/offsets/tints are first-pass and not headless-verifiable; expect tuning if any piece clips/sits oddly.

## Status: Upstream sync PR #11 OPEN (2026-06-21)

**davidhu0527/monecraft#11 OPEN** — `hutusi:main` → `davidhu0527:main`, **58 commits**, MERGEABLE (origin 0 behind upstream — clean lineage). Bundles everything since upstream's last merge (#9 living-world/fishing): status effects & potions (#28), XP & enchanting (#29), crafting hints + 3 fixes (#30), the v0.10.0 release, game modes (#31), pause-menu tabs (#32), difficulty (#33), hardcore (#34). Save schema **v5 → v10** (all additive pure-bump migrations; `readSave` chains v1→…→v10). David to review. NOTE: the prior sync attempt **#10 was CLOSED-unmerged** (it had tried status-effects/XP/crafting-hints; superseded by this fuller #11). `upstream`=`davidhu0527/monecraft`, `origin`=`hutusi/monecraft`. Branch cleanup DONE this session: all 7 merged origin feature/test branches deleted (`feat/endgame-ranged`, `feat/game-difficulty`, `feat/hardcore-mode`, `feature/camera-view-toggle`, `feature/procedural-audio`, `test/audio-regression-gaps`, `test/e2e-and-components`) — origin now just `main` + `entire/checkpoints/v1`.

## Status: Hardcore MERGED (2026-06-21)

**Hardcore — `hutusi/monecraft#34` MERGED** (2026-06-21, merge commit `3559cf6`; local branch deleted, `main` synced; **remote branch NOT deleted — pending user**). The LAST gameModes.ts-deferred axis — now **nothing deferred** (game modes → difficulty → hardcore all shipped). A per-world **immutable boolean** (not an enum/accessor module — just a flag threaded through). User chose the MOST faithful variant of all 3 design Qs: **spectate-the-dead-world** permadeath (not auto-delete/simple-gameover), **lock Survival + Hard** (not difficulty-only), **withered hearts** (cosmetic yes). Save **v9→v10** (additive `hardcore` + `gameOver` booleans; `migrateSaveV9toV10`), no worldgen change, zero assets. Engine: constructor resolves `hardcore` FIRST so it overrides mode/difficulty (forced Survival+Hard); a restored `gameOver` boots Spectator (the existing `!isNoclip` stuck-check leaves it un-teleported). The TWO lethal seams (`applyDamage`/`applyEnvironmentalDamage` arrow methods — poison/starvation-floored use `applyNonLethalDamage`, can't kill) divert to new **`GameEngine.triggerGameOver()`**: sets `gameOver`, switches to spectator DIRECTLY (bypassing the locked switch), leaves `isDead`/`respawnTimer` cleared so the respawn DeathScreen never shows. `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` no-op under hardcore; `pause` blocked during gameOver. Shell **force-saves on the `gameOver` event** (engine has no storage handle) so a tab-close still resumes the dead world. UI: CreateWorldForm hardcore toggle that locks the mode/difficulty grids (`disabled` + forced `effectiveMode`/`effectiveDifficulty`); PauseMenu disables both switchers; new **`GameOverScreen`** (mirrors VictoryScreen) with Spectate (minimizes to a corner badge)/Back-to-Worlds/Delete-World; new GameShell `onDeleteWorld` (deleteWorld + clear session + world-select). Withered hearts = 2 new PixelPalettes + 3 `heart_hardcore_*` HudIconNames in hudPixels.ts; StatusBars takes a `hardcore` prop + `sprite` override on the heart IconRow. 6 feature slices + a CodeRabbit-fix commit (`8f3ef37`). Gate green: lint/typecheck/format/**772 unit**/build + **17 e2e** (e2e save-assert 9→10; new menu e2e asserts hardcore boots locked survival+hard). **CodeRabbit (only reviewer) posted 2 quick-win findings, BOTH applied**: (1) `restoreGameOver` now requires `hardcore===true` too (a stray gameOver flag on a corrupt non-hardcore save can't lock it into spectator); (2) `sanitizeWorld`/`createWorld` normalize a hardcore WorldMeta's gameMode/difficulty to survival/hard (so contradictory persisted values can't leak to the world-card UI). Merged via **merge commit** (repo convention). NOT released/tagged — `[Unreleased]` now holds game modes + difficulty + hardcore. **NOTE: death→spectator visuals not headless-verifiable — a manual gameplay pass is recommended before the next release cut.**

## Status: Difficulty MERGED (2026-06-21)

**Difficulty — `hutusi/monecraft#33` MERGED** (2026-06-21, merge commit `9bc181b`; local branch `feat/game-difficulty` deleted, `main` synced; **remote branch NOT deleted — pending user** per the usual batch). The axis that game-modes #31 explicitly *deferred* (Peaceful) — now its own orthogonal dial **Peaceful/Easy/Normal/Hard** in new `lib/game/difficulties.ts` (enum + `isDifficulty` + `DIFFICULTY_PRESETS` + **accessor fns** `hostilesSpawn`/`mobDamageMultiplier`/`hostileSpawnIntervalScale`/`hostileCapScale`/`regenIntervalScale`/`starves`/`starvationFloorHp`, mirroring the gameMode predicate pattern). Save schema **v8→v9** (additive `difficulty`; `migrateSaveV8toV9`, default "normal"), no worldgen change, zero assets. Seams: `spawnDirector.ts` gates spawns on `hostilesSpawn` + scales cadence/cap (Peaceful=0, Easy×0.5→8, Normal=16, Hard×1.5→24); `mobAI.ts` multiplies every mob hit at the strike (0.5/1/1.5×, templates untouched); `playerStats.ts` scales regen (Peaceful ×0.5 = 2× faster) + runs the **NEW starvation tick** (first-ever: hunger 0 chips ½ heart every 4s to a per-level floor — Easy 10HP, Normal 1HP, Hard 0=death; Peaceful never). Peaceful switch despawns hostiles via a **plain splice** (no loot/XP/false-boss-victory) in `GameEngine.switchDifficulty`. The two axes don't cross-couple: spawning keys only on difficulty, damage/threat only on gameMode. UI: pickers in CreateWorldForm + PauseMenu Game tab (live `setDifficulty`). 8 feature slices + a menu-form-scroll CSS/e2e fix (the new picker pushed Create-World button off-screen) + **1 CodeRabbit-review-fix** (`c3d83e5`): clamped the night spawn wave `count` to remaining cap slots (a 2-pack roll at cap-1 overshot by 1, esp. lastPrompt: let's cut a new version then open the pr, what do you think?

content.text:
We just shipped v0.11.0 — and with it the game's combat/progression is now genuinely deep: 7 gear tiers, 11 enchantments, 9 potions/effects, an anvil/grindstone/enchanting loop, a boss. Three consecutive releases (#35 gear, #36 armor, #37 enchants/potions) have all been combat-and-gear focused.

So my read on the biggest gap: **the game is content-rich but goal-poor.** There's a huge amount to *do*, but almost nothing that gives players *direction* or rewards engaging with it — the only real objective is "beat the Dragon Lord." That's the highest-leverage thing to fix next, and it's a refreshing pivot away from more combat.

**My recommendation: Goals & progression meta — Advancements + Statistics.** A tree of advancements ("craft your first pickaxe," "enchant an item," "brew every potion," "survive a night," "defeat the Dragon Lord") plus a stats screen (blocks mined, mobs killed, distance walked, deaths). It makes *everything already in the game* pay off, guides new players through systems they'd otherwise miss, and is low-risk: additive save field, no worldgen change, mostly event-tracking (the engine already emits the events) + one new UI panel. It's the natural capstone after three content releases.

That said, the direction is yours — here are the credible alternatives:

content.text: Excellent choice — that's the highest-leverage gap. Let me ground the design by mapping the two surfaces this feature plugs into: the engine's event/state/save layer (the triggers + persistence) and the React shell (where a panel lives + how unlock toasts surface).

input.description: Map engine events, state, save, projection
input.prompt:
I'm planning an **Advancements (achievements) + Statistics** feature for "Monecraft", a Minecraft-inspired voxel game (Next.js/React/TypeScript/Three.js/Bun). The engine is a headless simulation (`lib/game/engine/`) that emits events and exposes immutable snapshots to React. Advancements unlock when the player does things (mine X, craft, enchant, brew, kill the boss, etc.); Statistics are running counters (blocks mined, mobs killed, distance walked, deaths, etc.). Both must persist in the save and surface to the UI.

Explore and report precisely (with file paths + symbol names) on these four things:

1. **The complete `GameEvent` union and every emit site.** Find the `GameEvent` type (likely in `lib/game/engine/state.ts`) and list every event variant. Then grep for `emit({ type:` (and `this.emit`) across `lib/game/engine/` to enumerate what events fire and where (e.g. blockBroken, blockPlaced, mobDied, mobHit, ateFood, drankPotion, enchanted, anvilCombined, grindstoneStripped, bossDefeated, pickedUp, died, etc.). These are the trigger surface for advancements and the increment points for stat counters. Note any events that carry useful payload (block id, mob kind, item ids).

2. **How persistent gameplay state is added to the save.** Read `lib/game/save.ts` and `lib/game/types.ts` (the SaveData type). Show how a top-level persistent field like `xp` is serialized/restored (the `xp` field, `restoreXp`, and how it's NOT cleared on death, unlike `effects`). I want the exact pattern to add a new persistent field (e.g. `stats` counters + `advancements` unlocked-id set) that survives death like xp does. Note the current save version (v12) and whether this needs a bump.

3. **How engine state is projected to React (the snapshot).** Find `GameSnapshot` and how the engine builds it each frame — especially how `xp`/`xpLevel` and `activeEffects` (effectsProjection) get from `GameState` into the snapshot that React reads via `useSyncExternalStore`. I want the pattern to surface unlocked advancements + stat counters (and a "just unlocked" one-shot for a toast).

4. **The engine step + command + GameState shape.** Show where mutable `GameState` is defined, how `GameState` holds things like `xp`/`effects`/`timers`, where the step loop and command dispatch live (`GameEngine.ts`), and how a one-shot event (like `enchanted` or `bossDefeated`) is emitted so the audio director / toasts react. I need to know where a stats-increment + advancement-check would hook in (ideally one chokepoint that observes emitted events, or per-event in dispatch/systems).

Report a structured summary: the event list (with payloads), the save persistence pattern (with the exact xp analog), the snapshot projection pattern, and the best hook point(s) for incrementing stats + checking advancement unlocks. Be very thorough and cite real paths/symbols.

input.description: Map React shell UI panels and toasts
input.prompt:
I'm planning an **Advancements (achievements) + Statistics** UI for "Monecraft", a Minecraft-inspired voxel game (Next.js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript). The React shell reads immutable snapshots from a headless engine via `useSyncExternalStore` and dispatches `Command`s. I need to know exactly where a new full-screen/overlay panel (an Advancements tab + a Statistics screen) should live, how it gets data, and how a transient "Advancement unlocked!" toast would surface.

Explore and report precisely (with file paths + symbol names) on these:

1. **The component/shell structure.** Map `components/` (especially `components/game/`). Find the top-level game UI component (likely `components/MinecraftGame.tsx` and/or `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`), how it reads the engine snapshot and renders HUD + panels. List the existing panels/screens and how each is toggled: the **InventoryPanel** (and its recipe book / Creative palette / crafting columns like EnchantingColumn/AnvilColumn), the **PauseMenu** (which has Game/Options/Controls tabs), and any full-screen overlays like **DeathScreen**, **VictoryScreen**, **GameOverScreen**. I want the pattern for adding a new panel — is it gated on an engine state flag (like `inventoryOpen`, `craftingStation`) or local React state?

2. **How panels open/close (input + commands).** Find how a key like `I` (inventory) opens a panel — trace the input handling (`lib/game/input/inputController.ts` and the command dispatch) and how the open/close state lives on `GameState`/`GameSnapshot` (e.g. `inventoryOpen`). I want to know how to wire a new key (Minecraft uses `L` for advancements) to open an Advancements/Stats overlay, and whether that should be engine state (a command + snapshot flag) or pure React UI state. Note the pointer-lock implications (opening a panel exits pointer lock).

3. **The toast / notification system.** Find how transient on-screen messages work — e.g. the `pickedUp` toast, save toasts, or any "Toast"/notification component. The audio director reacts to events; is there a parallel visual toast that listens to engine events (like `pickedUp`, `enchanted`)? I want the pattern to show an "Advancement unlocked: <name>" banner when the engine reports a newly-unlocked advancement.

4. **Existing presentational patterns to reuse.** How are item/block icons rendered in panels (e.g. `PixelImg`, `hudIconUrl`, sprite data URLs)? How does ActiveEffects render its icon+label chips? How does the recipe book lay out a grid of entries with locked/unlocked states (since advancements have a similar locked/unlocked + icon + description layout)? Cite the components I'd mirror.

Report a structured summary: the shell + panel-toggle pattern, the input→command→snapshot-flag flow for opening a panel, the toast pattern, and the reusable presentational components. Be very thorough and cite real paths/symbols.

content.text:
I've kicked off two parallel探索 passes to ground the design — one mapping the engine's event/state/save/projection layer (the advancement triggers + stat counters + persistence), the other mapping the React shell (where the panel lives, the open/close flow, and the unlock-toast pattern). They're running in the background; I'll fold their findings into a concrete, scoped plan as soon as they report back.

While that runs, here's the shape I'm expecting to propose, so you can react early:

- **Statistics** — a `stats` counter map on `GameState` (persisted like `xp`, *not* cleared on death), incremented at the events the engine already emits (`blockBroken`, `mobDied`, `drankPotion`, `enchanted`, distance from the motion tick, `died`, etc.). Surfaced read-only to a stats screen.
- **Advancements** — a static registry of advancement definitions (id, title, description, icon, trigger condition, optional parent for a small tree), an `unlocked` id-set on `GameState` (also persisted, death-proof), checked at the same event chokepoint; a one-shot "just unlocked" projection drives a toast + sound.
- **UI** — an Advancements/Stats overlay opened with a key (Minecraft uses **L**), reusing the recipe-book's locked/unlocked grid layout and the existing pixel-icon rendering; an "Advancement unlocked" toast reusing the existing notification path.
- **Save** — one additive top-level field (likely bundling `stats` + `advancements`); should be a clean additive bump with a pure migration, no worldgen impact.

Two things I'll want your call on once I've confirmed the plumbing (I'll ask concretely then): **how broad the first advancement set should be** (a tight ~12–15 covering each major system, vs. a larger tree), and **where the panel lives** (a dedicated `L`-key overlay like Minecraft, vs. a new tab in the existing pause menu). I'll come back shortly with the grounded plan.

step(dt: number, input: FrameInput): void {
  // Freeze during pause
  if (state.paused) {
    this.refreshSnapshot();
    return;
  }

  // Death: only mobs/respawn countdown tick
  if (state.isDead) {
    if (tickRespawnTimer(state, dt)) this.respawn();  // → emit("respawned")
    else {
      tickMobs(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);
      tickPrimedTnt(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);
      tickProjectiles(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);
    }
    this.refreshSnapshot();
    return;
  }

  // Sleeping: fade + time skip
  if (state.sleepTimer > 0) {
    state.sleepTimer = Math.max(0, state.sleepTimer - dt);
    if (state.sleepTimer === 0) this.wakeToMorning();  // → emit("wokeUp")
    this.refreshSnapshot();
    return;
  }

  // Live gameplay: 40+ tick subsystems in order
  const move = tickPlayerMotion(...);
  if (move.didJump) this.emit({type: "jumped"});
  if (move.didLand) this.emit({type: "landed", impact: ...});
  
  tickHungerDrain(state, move);
  tickHealthRegen(state, dt);
  tickStarvation(state, dt, this.applyStarvationFloored, this.applyEnvironmentalDamage);
  tickStatusEffects(state, dt, {applyPoisonDamage: this.applyPoisonDamage, emit: this.emit});
  tickWaterExposure(state, dt, this.applyEnvironmentalDamage);
  tickLavaExposure(state, dt, this.applyEnvironmentalDamage, hasEffect(state, "fire_resistance"));
  tickOxygen(state, dt, this.applyEnvironmentalDamage, hasEffect(state, "water_breathing"));
  
  tickMining(state, input, dt, this.emit, this.rng);
  tickThrownSpears(state, dt, this.removeMobAt, this.emit);
  tickFishing(state, dt, this.rng, this.emit);
  
  tickDayNight(state, dt);
  tickWeather(state);
  tickRandomBlocks(state, dt, this.rng);
  tickHostileSpawnDirector(state, dt, this.rng, this.surfaceYAt);
  tickSpawnerDirector(state, dt, this.rng, this.emit);  // ← emits mobSpawned
  tickMobs(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);                 // ← handles mobAttacked, mobDied
  tickPrimedTnt(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);            // ← emits explosion, tntPrimed
  tickProjectiles(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);          // ← emits arrowHit, mobHit
  tickBreeding(state, dt, this.rng, this.surfaceYAt, this.emit);
  
  this.refreshSnapshot();
}

step(dt: number, input: FrameInput): void {
  // Freeze during pause
  if (state.paused) {
    this.refreshSnapshot();
    return;
  }

  // Death: only mobs/respawn countdown tick
  if (state.isDead) {
    if (tickRespawnTimer(state, dt)) this.respawn();  // → emit("respawned")
    else {
      tickMobs(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);
      tickPrimedTnt(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);
      tickProjectiles(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);
    }
    this.refreshSnapshot();
    return;
  }

  // Sleeping: fade + time skip
  if (state.sleepTimer > 0) {
    state.sleepTimer = Math.max(0, state.sleepTimer - dt);
    if (state.sleepTimer === 0) this.wakeToMorning();  // → emit("wokeUp")
    this.refreshSnapshot();
    return;
  }

  // Live gameplay: 40+ tick subsystems in order
  const move = tickPlayerMotion(...);
  if (move.didJump) this.emit({type: "jumped"});
  if (move.didLand) this.emit({type: "landed", impact: ...});
  
  tickHungerDrain(state, move);
  tickHealthRegen(state, dt);
  tickStarvation(state, dt, this.applyStarvationFloored, this.applyEnvironmentalDamage);
  tickStatusEffects(state, dt, {applyPoisonDamage: this.applyPoisonDamage, emit: this.emit});
  tickWaterExposure(state, dt, this.applyEnvironmentalDamage);
  tickLavaExposure(state, dt, this.applyEnvironmentalDamage, hasEffect(state, "fire_resistance"));
  tickOxygen(state, dt, this.applyEnvironmentalDamage, hasEffect(state, "water_breathing"));
  
  tickMining(state, input, dt, this.emit, this.rng);
  tickThrownSpears(state, dt, this.removeMobAt, this.emit);
  tickFishing(state, dt, this.rng, this.emit);
  
  tickDayNight(state, dt);
  tickWeather(state);
  tickRandomBlocks(state, dt, this.rng);
  tickHostileSpawnDirector(state, dt, this.rng, this.surfaceYAt);
  tickSpawnerDirector(state, dt, this.rng, this.emit);  // ← emits mobSpawned
  tickMobs(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);                 // ← handles mobAttacked, mobDied
  tickPrimedTnt(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);            // ← emits explosion, tntPrimed
  tickProjectiles(state, dt, this.mobTickDeps);          // ← emits arrowHit, mobHit
  tickBreeding(state, dt, this.rng, this.surfaceYAt, this.emit);
  
  this.refreshSnapshot();
}

# Advancements + Statistics

## Context

Monecraft (v0.11.0, save v12) is now content-rich — 7 gear tiers, 11 enchantments,
9 potions/effects, an anvil/grindstone/enchanting loop, farming, breeding, fishing,
a boss — but **goal-poor**: the only objective is "beat the Dragon Lord," and new
players have no guided path through the systems. After three consecutive
combat/gear releases (#35/#36/#37), this adds the missing **progression meta**:

- **Statistics** — running counters (blocks mined, mobs killed, distance walked,
  deaths, items crafted/enchanted, potions drunk, fish caught, time played …).
- **Advancements** — a tight, flat set of ~15 achievements that unlock when the
  player engages each major system, with an unlock toast + chime.

Both **persist in the save and survive death** (like `xp`, not `effects`), surface
in a dedicated **`L`-key overlay** (two tabs), and add **zero binary assets** (icons
reuse existing item/block sprites). User-confirmed scope: **L-key overlay**, **tight
~15 flat set**.

## Design

### Engine — one chokepoint, declarative registry

Every gameplay event already funnels through `GameEngine.emit()`
(`lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts` ~L668; 29 event types in `lib/game/engine/state.ts`).
Hook a single observer there rather than editing 15 system files:

```
private emit = (event) => {
  this.events.push(event);
  if (event.type !== "advancementUnlocked") this.observeProgress(event); // guard recursion
};
private observeProgress(event) {
  recordEvent(this.state, event);                       // bump stat counters
  for (const id of evaluateAdvancements(this.state))    // locked-only, threshold met
    { this.state.advancements.add(id); this.emit({ type:"advancementUnlocked", id, name }); }
}
```

New module **`lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`**:
- `recordEvent(state, event)` — maps each event type to stat increments (e.g.
  `blockBroken`→`blocks_mined` + a per-ore counter for ore blocks; `mobDied`→
  `hostiles_killed` when the kind is hostile, via `MOB_TEMPLATES[kind].hostile`;
  `enchanted`→`items_enchanted`; `drankPotion`→`potions_drunk`; `fishingCaught`→
  `fish_caught`; `mobBred`→`animals_bred`; `bossDefeated`→`boss_defeated`;
  `crafted`→`items_crafted` + `crafted_<recipeId>`; `died`→`deaths`; `jumped`→`jumps`).
- `STATS` — display metadata for the Statistics tab (id → label).
- `ADVANCEMENTS` — **declarative** registry: `{ id, title, description, icon, category,
  stat, threshold }`. Unlock is uniformly `state.stats.get(stat) >= threshold`, so
  `evaluateAdvancements(state)` just iterates the not-yet-unlocked entries — trivially
  unit-testable. `icon` is an existing item/block id rendered via `itemIconUrl`
  (`lib/ui/sprites.ts`) — e.g. Diamonds!→`diamond_ore`, Enchanter→`enchanting_table`,
  Dragon Slayer→`dragon_heart` — **zero new assets**.
- Tick-driven display stats (`distance_walked` from `move.horizontalDistance`,
  `play_time` from `dt`) increment directly in `GameEngine.step()`; no advancement
  depends on them, so they stay out of the unlock path.

**Proposed ~15 advancements** (tunable; all map to detectable signals):
Getting Wood (mine a log), Stone Age (mine stone), Tool Up (craft a pickaxe),
Hot Topic (craft a furnace), Iron-ish (mine sliver ore), Diamonds! (mine diamond
ore), Take Aim (fire a bow — `bowFired`), Monster Hunter (kill a hostile), Two by
Two (breed animals), Time to Farm (harvest mature wheat — `blockBroken`
WheatStage3), Enchanter (enchant an item), Local Brewery (drink a potion), Sleep
Tight (`sleepStarted`), Hired Help (trade with a villager — `crafted` w/ a
`station:"villager"` recipe), Gone Fishing (`fishingCaught`), Dragon Slayer
(`bossDefeated`).

### New `crafted` event (small, broadly useful)

There is no craft event today. Add `{ type:"crafted"; recipeId:string }` to the
`GameEvent` union and emit it once in the `craft` command handler
(`GameEngine.dispatch`). Unlocks craft/brew/trade advancements + an `items_crafted`
stat; the audio director can ignore it.

### Persistence — save v12 → v13 (additive, death-proof)

Mirror the `xp` pattern exactly (`lib/game/save.ts` `restoreXp`; serialized in
`GameEngine.serialize`; restored in the constructor; **not** touched by
`clearEffects`):
- `GameState` += `stats: Map<string,number>`, `advancements: Set<string>`.
- `SaveData` (`lib/game/types.ts`) += `stats?: Array<{id:string;value:number}>`,
  `advancements?: string[]`; bump to `version: 13`.
- `save.ts`: `serializeStats`/`restoreStats` + `restoreAdvancements` (finite ≥0
  values, string ids; mirror `serializeEffects`/`restoreEffects` at L334–353),
  `migrateSaveV12toV13` pure bump, extend the `readSave` v1→…→v13 chain.
  `SAVE_KEY` unchanged; **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8**.

### UI — dedicated `L`-key overlay

- Engine flag: `GameState.advancementsOpen` + project `advancementsOpen:boolean`
  and a low-churn `advancementsUnlocked:number` (count) into `GameSnapshot`
  (both primitives — safe under the per-key `!==` compare in `refreshSnapshot`).
- `Command` += `{ type:"toggleAdvancements" }`; `GameEngine.dispatch` toggles the
  flag (mirror `toggleInventory`).
- Input: `KeyL` handler in `lib/game/input/inputController.ts` (mirror the `KeyI`
  block — dispatch, clear keys, exit pointer lock).
- `GameApi` (`lib/game/engine/state.ts`) += `advancementState(): { stats:
  Array<{id,value}>; unlocked: string[] }` so the panel reads detail **on render**
  via `snapshot.api` — avoids per-frame snapshot churn; the panel re-renders
  whenever the snapshot changes (frequent during play) and on every unlock.
- New `components/game/AdvancementsPanel.tsx`, rendered in
  `components/MinecraftGame.tsx` when `snapshot.advancementsOpen` (mirror the
  `inventoryOpen` backdrop+panel block). Two tabs (PauseMenu tab pattern): an
  **Advancements** grid grouped by category with locked/unlocked styling (mirror
  the recipe-book grid in `InventoryPanel.tsx` + `PixelImg`/`ItemIcon`) and a
  **Statistics** list. CSS in `app/hud.css` mirroring `.pause-overlay`/`.recipe-*`.
- Toast: listen for `advancementUnlocked` in the `useMinecraftGame` event-drain
  loop (~L293–329) → `flashMessage(\`Advancement Unlocked: ${event.name}\`)`
  (the `pickedUp` pattern). Audio: a chime in `lib/game/audio/audioDirector.ts`.

## Files

- New: `lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts` (recordEvent, STATS,
  ADVANCEMENTS, evaluateAdvancements) + `.test.ts`;
  `components/game/AdvancementsPanel.tsx` + `.test.tsx`.
- Engine: `lib/game/engine/state.ts` (GameState/GameSnapshot/GameEvent/GameApi),
  `lib/game/engine/commands.ts`, `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts` (emit observer,
  step tick-stats, dispatch toggle + `crafted` emit, serialize/restore, snapshot).
- Save: `lib/game/types.ts`, `lib/game/save.ts` (v13 + migration + (de)serialize).
- Input/UI: `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`, `components/MinecraftGame.tsx`,
  `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts` (toast), `app/hud.css`,
  `lib/game/audio/audioDirector.ts`.
- Reuse: `itemIconUrl` (`lib/ui/sprites.ts`), `PixelImg`/`ItemIcon`, the recipe-book
  grid + PauseMenu tab patterns, `MOB_TEMPLATES` (`lib/game/mobs.ts`) for hostility.

### Commit slices (branch `feat/advancements`)

1. `feat(stats): track gameplay statistics` — stats Map + recordEvent + step
   tick-stats + the `crafted` event + save v13 persistence of `stats`; tests.
2. `feat(advancements): registry + unlock tracking` — ADVANCEMENTS, the emit
   observer, `advancementUnlocked` event, `advancements` Set persistence; tests.
3. `feat(ui): advancements & statistics overlay (L key)` — flag/command/KeyL,
   GameApi accessor, AdvancementsPanel + tabs + CSS, toast + chime; component/e2e.
4. `docs` — reference (advancements + stats tables), manual (open with L; what
   unlocks), save-format (v13), adding-content (new "An advancement / a stat"
   section — the extension pattern), testing.md coverage, CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`.

## Verification

- Full CI `verify` gate green (`lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test`,
  `build`) + `bun run test:e2e` (renderer/shell touched).
- Engine tests (`advancements.test.ts`): `recordEvent` bumps the right counter per
  event (incl. per-ore + hostile-only kill); `evaluateAdvancements` unlocks exactly
  at the threshold, never twice, and is order-independent; the `crafted` event
  drives `items_crafted`/trade unlock.
- `GameEngine.test.ts`: a headless run that breaks an ore / kills a hostile / enchants
  / drinks a potion / defeats the boss emits `advancementUnlocked` once each and the
  stats reflect it; **a full save round-trip preserves stats + advancements and they
  survive a death** (assert not cleared, unlike effects).
- `save.test.ts`: `migrateSaveV12toV13` pure bump; `serializeStats`/`restoreStats`/
  `restoreAdvancements` round-trip + drop garbage; the v1→…→v13 chain. Update the
  e2e save-version assertion 12 → 13.
- Component test (`AdvancementsPanel.test.tsx`): renders locked vs unlocked entries,
  switches tabs, shows stat values. e2e: press `L` → overlay opens (pointer lock
  released) → close.
- Manual pass (not headless-verifiable): the overlay layout/icons and the unlock
  toast + chime.

# Advancements + Statistics

## Context

Monecraft (v0.11.0, save v12) is now content-rich — 7 gear tiers, 11 enchantments,
9 potions/effects, an anvil/grindstone/enchanting loop, farming, breeding, fishing,
a boss — but **goal-poor**: the only objective is "beat the Dragon Lord," and new
players have no guided path through the systems. After three consecutive
combat/gear releases (#35/#36/#37), this adds the missing **progression meta**:

- **Statistics** — running counters (blocks mined, mobs killed, distance walked,
  deaths, items crafted/enchanted, potions drunk, fish caught, time played …).
- **Advancements** — a tight, flat set of ~15 achievements that unlock when the
  player engages each major system, with an unlock toast + chime.

Both **persist in the save and survive death** (like `xp`, not `effects`), surface
in a dedicated **`L`-key overlay** (two tabs), and add **zero binary assets** (icons
reuse existing item/block sprites). User-confirmed scope: **L-key overlay**, **tight
~15 flat set**.

## Design

### Engine — one chokepoint, declarative registry

Every gameplay event already funnels through `GameEngine.emit()`
(`lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts` ~L668; 29 event types in `lib/game/engine/state.ts`).
Hook a single observer there rather than editing 15 system files:

```
private emit = (event) => {
  this.events.push(event);
  if (event.type !== "advancementUnlocked") this.observeProgress(event); // guard recursion
};
private observeProgress(event) {
  recordEvent(this.state, event);                       // bump stat counters
  for (const id of evaluateAdvancements(this.state))    // locked-only, threshold met
    { this.state.advancements.add(id); this.emit({ type:"advancementUnlocked", id, name }); }
}
```

New module **`lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`**:
- `recordEvent(state, event)` — maps each event type to stat increments (e.g.
  `blockBroken`→`blocks_mined` + a per-ore counter for ore blocks; `mobDied`→
  `hostiles_killed` when the kind is hostile, via `MOB_TEMPLATES[kind].hostile`;
  `enchanted`→`items_enchanted`; `drankPotion`→`potions_drunk`; `fishingCaught`→
  `fish_caught`; `mobBred`→`animals_bred`; `bossDefeated`→`boss_defeated`;
  `crafted`→`items_crafted` + `crafted_<recipeId>`; `died`→`deaths`; `jumped`→`jumps`).
- `STATS` — display metadata for the Statistics tab (id → label).
- `ADVANCEMENTS` — **declarative** registry: `{ id, title, description, icon, category,
  stat, threshold }`. Unlock is uniformly `state.stats.get(stat) >= threshold`, so
  `evaluateAdvancements(state)` just iterates the not-yet-unlocked entries — trivially
  unit-testable. `icon` is an existing item/block id rendered via `itemIconUrl`
  (`lib/ui/sprites.ts`) — e.g. Diamonds!→`diamond_ore`, Enchanter→`enchanting_table`,
  Dragon Slayer→`dragon_heart` — **zero new assets**.
- Tick-driven display stats (`distance_walked` from `move.horizontalDistance`,
  `play_time` from `dt`) increment directly in `GameEngine.step()`; no advancement
  depends on them, so they stay out of the unlock path.

**Proposed ~15 advancements** (tunable; all map to detectable signals):
Getting Wood (mine a log), Stone Age (mine stone), Tool Up (craft a pickaxe),
Hot Topic (craft a furnace), Iron-ish (mine sliver ore), Diamonds! (mine diamond
ore), Take Aim (fire a bow — `bowFired`), Monster Hunter (kill a hostile), Two by
Two (breed animals), Time to Farm (harvest mature wheat — `blockBroken`
WheatStage3), Enchanter (enchant an item), Local Brewery (drink a potion), Sleep
Tight (`sleepStarted`), Hired Help (trade with a villager — `crafted` w/ a
`station:"villager"` recipe), Gone Fishing (`fishingCaught`), Dragon Slayer
(`bossDefeated`).

### New `crafted` event (small, broadly useful)

There is no craft event today. Add `{ type:"crafted"; recipeId:string }` to the
`GameEvent` union and emit it once in the `craft` command handler
(`GameEngine.dispatch`). Unlocks craft/brew/trade advancements + an `items_crafted`
stat; the audio director can ignore it.

### Persistence — save v12 → v13 (additive, death-proof)

Mirror the `xp` pattern exactly (`lib/game/save.ts` `restoreXp`; serialized in
`GameEngine.serialize`; restored in the constructor; **not** touched by
`clearEffects`):
- `GameState` += `stats: Map<string,number>`, `advancements: Set<string>`.
- `SaveData` (`lib/game/types.ts`) += `stats?: Array<{id:string;value:number}>`,
  `advancements?: string[]`; bump to `version: 13`.
- `save.ts`: `serializeStats`/`restoreStats` + `restoreAdvancements` (finite ≥0
  values, string ids; mirror `serializeEffects`/`restoreEffects` at L334–353),
  `migrateSaveV12toV13` pure bump, extend the `readSave` v1→…→v13 chain.
  `SAVE_KEY` unchanged; **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8**.

- Engine flag: `GameState.advancementsOpen` + project `advancementsOpen:boolean`

- `Command` += `{ type:"toggleAdvancements" }`; `GameEngine.dispatch` toggles the
  flag (mirror `toggleInventory`).
- Input: `KeyL` handler in `lib/game/input/inputController.ts` (mirror the `KeyI`
  block — dispatch, clear keys, exit pointer lock).
- `GameApi` (`lib/game/engine/state.ts`) += `advancementState(): { stats:

  **Advancements** grid grouped by category with locked/unlocked styling (mirror
  the recipe-book grid in `InventoryPanel.tsx` + `PixelImg`/`ItemIcon`) and a
  **Statistics** list. CSS in `app/hud.css` mirroring `.pause-overlay`/`.recipe-*`.
